'''Cristian Sorin Calude''' (born 21 April 1952) is a New Zealand mathematician and [[computer scientist]].<ref>[https://dblp.org/pid/c/CSCalude Publications] at [[DBLP]]</ref>

==Biography==
After graduating from the [[Vasile Alecsandri National College (Galați)|Vasile Alecsandri National College]] in [[Galați]], he studied at the [[University of Bucharest]], where he was student of
[[Grigore C. Moisil]] and [[Solomon Marcus]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://calude.net/cristianscalude/about/about-vitae|title=Cristian S. Calude: Vitae|access-date=4 September 2021}}</ref> Calude received his [[Ph.D.]] in Mathematics from the University of Bucharest under the direction of Solomon Marcus in 1977.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=35458}}</ref>

He is currently chair professor at the [[University of Auckland]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.science.auckland.ac.nz/people/profile/c-calude |title=Staff profile page at the university of Auckland| website=www.cs.auckland.ac.nz}}</ref> New Zealand and also the founding director of the Centre for Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cs.auckland.ac.nz/research/groups/CDMTCS/|title=Research Groups – CDMTCS|website=www.cs.auckland.ac.nz}}</ref> Visiting professor in many universities in Europe, North and South America, Australasia, South Africa, including [[Monbusho]] Visiting professor, [[JAIST]], 1999 and visiting professor [[École Normale Supérieure|ENS]], Paris, 2009, [[École Polytechnique]], Paris, 2011; visiting fellow, [[Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences]], 2012; guest professor, [[Sun Yat-sen University]], [[Guangzhou]], China, 2017–2020; visiting fellow [[ETH]] Zurich, 2019. Former professor at the [[University of Bucharest]]. Calude is author or co-author of more than 270 research articles and 8 books,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/Books-Cristian-S-Calude/s?ie=UTF8&page=1&rh=n:283155,p_27:Cristian+S+Calude|title=Calude Calude's books at Amazon|website=www.amazon.com}}</ref> and is cited by more than 550 authors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cs.auckland.ac.nz/~cristian/quotations.html |title=Calude's citations|website=www.cs.auckland.ac.nz}}</ref>
He is known for research in [[algorithmic information theory]], [[quantum computing]], [[discrete mathematics]] and the [[History of computation|history and]] [[philosophy of computation]].<ref>{{cite book | last=Marcus | first=Solomon | editor-last1=Dinneen|editor-first1=M. J.|editor-last2=Khoussainov|editor-first2=B.|editor-last3=Nies|editor-first3=A.|title=Computation, Physics and Beyond | chapter=The Art of Reaching the Age of Sixty | series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science | publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg | publication-place=Berlin, Heidelberg | volume=7160 | date=2012 | isbn=978-3-642-27653-8 | doi=10.1007/978-3-642-27654-5_1 | page=1–19}}</ref>

In 2017, together with Sanjay Jain, [[Bakhadyr Khoussainov]], Wei Li, and Frank Stephan, he announced an algorithm for deciding [[parity games]] in [[quasipolynomial time]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.comp.nus.edu.sg/~sanjay/paritygame.pdf|title= Deciding Parity Games in Quasipolynomial Time|access-date=20 August 2022}}</ref> Their result was presented by [[Bakhadyr Khoussainov]] at the [[Symposium on Theory of Computing]] 2017<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://acm-stoc.org/stoc2017/STOC2017accepted.pdf|title=STOC 2017 Accepted Papers|access-date=20 August 2022}}</ref> and won a Best Paper Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sigact.org/prizes/best_paper.html|title=ACM SIGACT – STOC Best Paper Award|website=www.sigact.org}}</ref>

Calude was awarded the [[National Order of Faithful Service]] in the degree of Knight<ref name="auto">{{Cite web | url=https://www.presidency.ro/ro/media/comunicate-de-presa/decret-de-decorare-semnat-de-presedintele-romaniei-domnul-klaus-iohannis1561627179 |title = Decret de decorare semnat de Președintele României, domnul Klaus Iohannis}}</ref> by the [[President of Romania]], [[Klaus Iohannis]], in June 2019.

In 2021, together with Sanjay Jain, [[Bakhadyr Khoussainov]], Wei Li, and Frank Stephan, he won the [[Nerode Prize|EATCS Nerode Prize]]<ref>[https://eatcs.org/index.php/nerode-prize IPEC Nerode Prize]</ref> for their [[Time complexity#Polynomial time|quasipolynomial time algorithm]] for deciding [[parity games]].

Calude has [[Erdős Number]] 2 via to [[Solomon Marcus]].

==Distinctions and prizes==
*"Computing Reviews Award", [[Association for Computing Machinery]], New York City, 1986.
*"Gheorghe Lazăr" Mathematics Prize, [[Romanian Academy]], Romania, 1988.
*Excellence in Research Award, University of Bucharest, Romania, 2007.
*Dean's Award for Excellence in Teaching, University of Auckland, 2007.
*[[Hood Fellow]], 2008–2009.
*Member of the [[Academia Europaea]], 2008.<ref>[https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Calude_Cristian Cristian S. Calude], ae-info.org</ref>
*Romanian [[National Order of Faithful Service]] in the degree of Knight,<ref name="auto"/> June 2019.
*"EATCS-IPEC [[Nerode Prize]]", 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://eatcs.org/index.php/nerode-prize|title= Nerode Prize|publisher= EATCS}}</ref>
*"Doctor Honoris Causa, Apolonia University, Iasi, Romania", 2023, <ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.univapollonia.ro|title=Apolonia University, Iasi}}</ref>
*"Full Member SIGMA XI", 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sigmaxi.org|title= SIGMA XI}}</ref>
